newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas stocks surge, ending ahead on foreign bids.
newsitem.headline: Caracas stocks surge, ending ahead on foreign bids.

text.p: Caracas stocks surged as foreign bidders returned to the market, snapping-up blue chips on signs labor strife may finally be on the wane, traders said.
The market's leading 19-share index closed ahead 2.09 percent at 6,521.72 points as 35.4 million shares traded worth 4.1 billion bolivars ($8.6 million).
"Investment banks continue to recommend Venezuelan stocks and that's bringing foreigners back," said InverUnion broker Hector Perez.
The government reached a 35 percent pay rise pre-accord Wednesday with the Confederation of Venezuelan Workers (CTV), Venezuela's largest public sector union.

"Labor strife has been the single most worrying factor for foreign investors this year," said Santander analyst Jose Corral. "Once it's finally settled, we see huge growth for the bolsa -- 32 percent in dollar terms for the year."
The pre-accord still has to be agreed with other unions.
In the day, among traded stocks, 18 rose, 15 fell and 13 closed flat.

Among the day's strongest gainers, foods company Mavesa closed ahead 4.80 bolivars at 154.00, utility Electricidad de Caracas rose 4.80 bolivars finishing at 154.00, while national telephone company CANTV gained 45.25 bolivars to finish at 2045.25 bolivars.
